classification.difficultyReason: Distinguishes replacement from non-replacement, adds probabilities for either order, and uses a complement.

children.label: a
children.prompt: A bag contains 2 red marbles and 3 black marbles. Two marbles are drawn from the bag. Each marble is replaced after it is drawn and the bag is shaken. Find the probability of selecting:

answer.worked:
Replacement keeps the probability of black at $\frac35$ on each draw.
$$\begin{align*}P(BB)&=\frac35\times\frac35\\P(BB)&=\frac9{25}\end{align*}$$

Replacement keeps the probability of red at $\frac25$ on each draw.
$$\begin{align*}P(RR)&=\frac25\times\frac25\\P(RR)&=\frac4{25}\end{align*}$$

children.label: iii
children.prompt: a red and a black marble

answer.worked:
The two possible orders are $RB$ and $BR$.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{one of each})&=\frac25\times\frac35+\frac35\times\frac25\\P(\text{one of each})&=\frac6{25}+\frac6{25}\\P(\text{one of each})&=\frac{12}{25}\end{align*}$$

The complement is selecting two black marbles.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{at least one red})&=1-\frac35\times\frac35\\P(\text{at least one red})&=1-\frac9{25}\\P(\text{at least one red})&=\frac{16}{25}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: From the same bag of marbles as in part a, two marbles are selected without replacing the first marble. Find the probability that the selection contains:

answer.worked:
After a red is selected, 1 red remains among 4 marbles.
$$\begin{align*}P(RR)&=\frac25\times\frac14\\P(RR)&=\frac1{10}\end{align*}$$

children.label: ii
children.prompt: a black and a red marble

answer.worked:
The two possible orders are $BR$ and $RB$. There are 4 marbles left for the second draw.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{one of each})&=\frac35\times\frac24+\frac25\times\frac34\\P(\text{one of each})&=\frac6{20}+\frac6{20}\\P(\text{one of each})&=\frac35\end{align*}$$

children.label: iii
children.prompt: two marbles of the same colour

answer.worked:
The disjoint possibilities are $RR$ and $BB$.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{same colour})&=\frac25\times\frac14+\frac35\times\frac24\\P(\text{same colour})&=\frac2{20}+\frac6{20}\\P(\text{same colour})&=\frac25\end{align*}$$
